quotes.text: Adopt the push-up position with your hands roughly shoulder-width apart. Brace your core and pull your shoulders down and back.
Start from a high plank position with your hands shoulder-width apart.
Start in a downward dog yoga position with hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart and your body forming an inverted V-shape.
Keeping your legs straight, lift your butt into the air so your body resembles an inverted V.
Move your hands closer to your feet to put more weight on your hands and achieve a more inverted position.
Lift your hips up and back to form an upside down V with your body.
Keeping your hips up, bend your arms and lower your head to within an inch of the floor. Tuck your elbows inward as you descend.
Lower your head toward the floor by bending your elbows, descending until your head nearly touches the floor. Keep your elbows at approximately 45 degrees from your body.
Push back up until your arms are straight, and repeat.
Press your body upward by extending your elbows, returning to the pike position. Avoid locking out your elbows at the top to maintain continuous tension in the deltoids.
Keep your neck neutral with your chin slightly tucked. Do not lift your head and hyperextend your neck.
You want to move your head forward and down as you bend your elbows, maintaining a neutral neck and spine from start to finish.
Keep your head neutral and focus forward to maintain proper spinal alignment.
Moving only your head toward the floor, similar to the handstand push-up, often leads to elbow flaring, poor movement mechanics, and—you guessed it—an increased risk of injury.
Letting your elbows flare out isn’t just poor movement mechanics. Doing this can contribute to shoulder impingement and, in the most severe cases, lead to a rotator cuff tear down the line.
Elbows flaring too wide, which increases shoulder stress and reduces effectiveness
“As with the regular push-up, you’ll want to keep your elbows tucked into your body while you move through the pike push-up,” says Kate.

“Letting them flare out to your sides is often a sign that your triceps are being overloaded. Instead of eking out shoddy reps, you should consider scaling down to standard push-ups or modified push-ups from your knees.”

Develop adequate upper body and shoulder strength through traditional and incline push-ups before progressing to pike variations.
Perform 3 sets of 5-12 repetitions, adjusting based on fitness level and strength.
I typically recommend starting with something comfortable, even if it’s only one or two reps at a time. Do a few low-rep sets, then aim to increase the number of reps by one or two the next week.
If you can do a few sets of ten or more reps with good form, you are probably ready to move up a level and try a more demanding pike push-up variation.
if the next variation feels too overly hard, or you cannot do it properly, it’s okay to return to your previous level
